plan.chapterName: OpenStax Organic Chemistry, chapter 5: Stereochemistry at Tetrahedral Centers
plan.contextChunk: This figure pairs a flat structural drawing with a three-dimensional model of the same molecule, both cut by a horizontal plane. On the left, two carbons lettered "C" sit one above the other, joined by a vertical bond. The upper carbon bears an "H" above it on a dashed bond, an "HO" group at the left in magenta on a bold wedge, and a "CO2H" group at the right in green. The lower carbon repeats that arrangement flipped vertically: "HO" again at the left and "CO2H" at the right, but its "H" now points downward on a dashed bond. A pale blue parallelogram drawn edge-on slices horizontally between the two carbons, labeled "Symmetry plane". On the right the molecule appears as a ball-and-stick model, two dark gray carbons stacked vertically, each carrying a small blue sphere, a red oxygen with a second red sphere beyond it, and a branching green group, with an identical pale blue plane passing between them. Running the plane through both depictions asks the reader to check one half against the other. Because the halves are reflections, the molecule proves superimposable on its own mirror image despite having two chirality centers, the situation that defines a meso compound.

elements: flat 2D structural formula (left panel): two lettered C atoms stacked vertically, joined by a vertical bond
upper carbon substituents: 'H' label above on a dashed wedge bond, 'HO' label left in magenta on a bold wedge bond, 'CO2H' label right in green on a plain bond
lower carbon substituents mirrored vertically: 'H' below on dashed wedge, 'HO' left in magenta on bold wedge, 'CO2H' right in green
pale blue parallelogram drawn edge-on slicing horizontally between the two carbons, labeled 'Symmetry plane'
ball-and-stick model (right panel): two dark gray carbon spheres stacked vertically, joined by a stick bond
small blue spheres (hydrogens) attached to each carbon, upper one pointing up/behind, lower one down/behind
on each carbon a red oxygen sphere with a smaller red sphere (OH hydrogen) beyond it, pointing left
on each carbon a branching green carboxyl group (CO2H): a green sphere bonded to two further green spheres
identical pale blue translucent plane passing horizontally between the two carbon spheres of the model
stick bonds connecting all model atoms

interactions.label: Representation
interactions.teaches: The same internal mirror plane cuts both the flat drawing and the 3D model — the reflection that makes the molecule achiral exists in every representation, so recognizing a meso compound does not depend on how it is drawn

Clicking an HO, H, or CO2H group on one stereocenter highlights its reflected counterpart on the other stereocenter across the plane, showing every substituent has an exact mirror partner so the two halves' handedness cancels
Rotating the ball-and-stick model reveals that the two halves really are 3D mirror images — the wedge/dash depth cues in the flat drawing correspond to actual above/below-plane positions

demo_steps.title: Both views with the plane
demo_steps.narration: The structural formula and the ball-and-stick model appear side by side, both sliced by the same pale blue symmetry plane between the two carbons.

demo_steps.title: Structure only
demo_steps.narration: Isolate the flat drawing: each HO, H, and CO2H above the plane has an identical partner below it. Click a group to see its reflection highlight across the plane.

demo_steps.title: Model only
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the 3D model: the blue, red, and green spheres above the plane mirror those below it in true 3D. Orbit to confirm the reflection from other angles — this is why the molecule is meso and achiral despite two chirality centers.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Molecule is a meso tartaric-acid-like structure: two tetrahedral carbons ~1.5 units apart along +Y, upper C at y=+0.75, lower C at y=-0.75, joined by a vertical bond. Each carbon carries four substituents tetrahedrally (109.5°): H (small sphere r≈0.25, blue #4477cc in the model; dashed wedge going away in the drawing — upper H up, lower H down), OH (red #cc2222 oxygen r≈0.45 with smaller red H r≈0.2 beyond it, pointing left, wedge toward viewer in the drawing, magenta label #cc0099), and CO2H (green #2d9e4f: central sphere r≈0.45 bonded to two terminal green spheres r≈0.4, pointing right, green label). Carbon spheres r≈0.5, dark gray #555555. The symmetry plane is a horizontal (XZ) plane at y=0, pale blue #a8d8f0 at ~0.35 opacity, spanning roughly 6×4 units, drawn edge-on as a parallelogram strip in the 2D panel with the label 'Symmetry plane' to its right. Every substituent above the plane must be the exact mirror image (negate y) of its counterpart below — equal sizes for equal groups. The 2D structural panel is a flat front-on overlay: black 'C' letters, magenta 'HO', green 'CO2H', dark 'H' labels, bold wedges toward viewer for the HO groups, dashed wedges for the H's. Whole scene spans about ±3 units in x and z, ±3 in y.
interactionPlan.notes: Keep the 2D structural formula as a billboarded flat group and the ball-and-stick model as a true 3D group; the toggle shows structure only, model only, or both side by side (overlay), with the translucent plane persisting in all three. For click-selection, raycast against all substituent spheres and the 2D text labels; on click, apply a highlight (emissive boost or outline) to the clicked group and its y-mirrored counterpart, clearing any previous selection. Build the model by constructing the upper half and explicitly mirroring y-coordinates for the lower half to guarantee the reflection is exact.

authoredContext:
The 2R,3S and 2S,3R structures are identical because the molecule has a plane of symmetry and is therefore achiral. The symmetry plane cuts through the C2–C3 bond, making one half of the molecule a mirror image of the other half (the figure). Because of the plane of symmetry, the molecule is achiral, despite the fact that it has two chirality centers. Such compounds, which are achiral, yet contain chirality centers, are called meso compounds (me-zo). Thus, tartaric acid exists in three stereoisomeric forms: two enantiomers and one meso form.

A symmetry plane through the C2–C3 bond of meso-tartaric acid makes the molecule achiral.

The wedge-dash structure and ball-and-stick model of tartaric acid. C2 and C3 have a horizontal symmetry plane.

Some physical properties of the three stereoisomers are listed in the table. The (+)- and (−)-tartaric acids have identical melting points, solubilities, and densities, but they differ in the sign of their rotation of plane-polarized light. The meso isomer, by contrast, is diastereomeric with the (+) and (−) forms. It has no mirror-image relationship to (+)- and (−)-tartaric acids, is a different compound altogether, and thus has different physical properties.

discrepancies: In the source the flat structure and the ball-and-stick model are cleanly separated side-by-side panels; in the default Overlay view the two representations crowd and partially overlap, with the pale-blue planes and duplicated 'Symmetry plane' labels colliding in the middle
The 2D structural formula is rendered slightly tilted in 3D space rather than flat/front-on as in the source, making the wedge/dash stereobonds harder to read
Two separate 'Symmetry plane' labels appear (one per representation) and they overlap the model geometry, whereas the source has a single label beside one plane

The ball-and-stick model's substituent arrangement is roughly right but the CO2H branch is rendered as three loose green spheres without the source's clear carboxyl cluster geometry, and the OH groups show an odd big-red/small-red pairing
evaluation.notes: Strong pedagogy: correct meso/mirror-plane concept, functional view toggles, guided tour, and click-to-highlight mirror partners; main weakness is cluttered overlapping layout in the default Overlay mode and slightly odd substituent geometry.
action_items: Increase horizontal separation between the structure panel and the model (or default to a cleaner single view) so planes and labels do not overlap
Render the flat structure panel front-on (no tilt) to match the source's 2D drawing
Use a single 'Symmetry plane' label, or offset the two labels so they do not collide with the model
Refine the CO2H cluster to read as a carboxyl group (central carbon with two oxygens + OH) rather than three identical green spheres

feedback.rationale: Concept accuracy and interactivity are perfect (5/5) with a 4.4 average, no failure modes, and the remaining discrepancies are minor layout polish — the figure is good enough to stop iterating.
